newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse still looking for higher turnover.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse still looking for higher turnover.

text.p: Polish shares could rise on Monday, analysts said, but they were divided on whether there would be higher turnover next week to trigger a significant growth trend.
The main market's WIG index inched up this week to 13,932.0 points, up 0.3 percent from last Friday's close, with turnovers low at around 80 million on both markets for most of the week. @

Some analysts said the previous week's 9.3-percent rise in turnovers over 110 million zlotys, buoyed by firms' better July earnings reports, was the start of a growth trend that might continue next week after this week's correction.
Others termed last week's jump the correction, saying the market could return to falls begun on July 5 at 14,282.2 points after the market had surged nearly 90 percent this year to a 27-month high.
"We could have growth on Monday... but I'm not inclined to believe we'll beat our July high next week," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage. @
Markiewicz said a bad sign was the apparent speculative growth of smaller stocks on Friday, when the parallel market of less liquid issues surged by 4.3 percent.
But analysts said there were reasons to believe the market would pierce the recent high later in September.
"The summer vacation is ending, the business cycle is improving and prices are not too high," said Grzegorz Sawicki, an analyst at Penetrator brokerage.
Last week firms published slightly better July earnings reports after a disappointing first half. Industrial production also grew by 4.8 percent in July. @

Analysts also said flat food prices in August's second third which were released this week could keep the month's inflation at around 0.5 percent, providing grounds for a possible interest-rate cut as early as late September.
They also said some of the money from the recent $23.7- million-zloty oversubscription of the Kompap paper firm's public offering could give stocks a slight boost next week.

Krosno, led main market gainers this week, up 16.3 percent, followed by Petrobank, up 10.7 percent, possibly lifted by the interior ministry's clearance on Thursday of a majority-stake sale to South Korea's LG Group. @
Friday's news of total foreign direct investment rising to about $10 billion since 1990 from $6.8 million at the end of last year was also a good sign, analysts said.
